supporting_quotes: In the following we present a short overview of the implementation for the three pipeline steps for NER, ER, and RE.

we describe the extraction of process elements and of relations between them as instances of three sub-problems of information extraction, which are Named Entity Recognition (NER), Relation Extraction (RE), and Entity Resolution (ER).
The PET dataset contains relation information on mention level, which allows our approach to learn on local level.
criterion_assessments.notes: Directly ties NLP information extraction to process element extraction and relation extraction.

supporting_quotes: The NER step is identical to the implementation from [7]. The approach is based on Conditional Random Fields [23].
We implemented two modules for the ER step, namely a naive ER method, and a method based on pre-trained end-to-end neural coreference resolution, as described in [13] and implemented in spaCy.
The naive ER method, which we will call naive ER for short, iteratively selects the best matching mentions with identical NER tags.
The pre-trained end-to-end neural coreference resolution module, which we will call neural ER from now on, predicts co-referent spans of text, i.e. spans of text referring to each other.
We call this module BoostRelEx for short in following sections.
For each combination of head and tail mention of a relation we build features containing tags, distance in tokens and in sentences between them, and a number c of neighboring mention tags as context.
This feature set is then presented to the model, which predicts a class for it.

We train the BoostRelEx module for i = 1000 iterations, which is the most computationally intensive step in the whole pipeline, taking about 25 minutes on an Intel i9-9900K CPU @ 3.60GHz, using a negative sampling rate rn = 40 and context size of c = 2.
The PET dataset contains total of 45 documents, with seven entity types, and six relation types.

We compare our pipeline to the current state of the art of information extraction on PET and show that we outperform it in five out of six relation types, with an absolute increase of 6% in F1 scores.
criterion_assessments.notes: Provides concrete pipeline description, CRF/ER/RE methods, neural coreference, BoostRelEx, and empirical validation with comparative results.

Abstract. The extraction of business processes elements from textual documents is a research area which still lacks the ability to scale to the variety of real-world texts.

In this paper we investigate the usage of pre-trained language models and in-context learning to address the problem of information extraction from process description documents as a way to exploit the power of deep learning approaches while relying on few annotated data.

Abstract. The extraction of business processes elements from textual documents is a research area which still lacks the ability to scale to the variety of real-world texts.

In this paper we investigate the usage of pre-trained language models and in-context learning to address the problem of information extraction from process description documents as a way to exploit the power of deep learning approaches while relying on few annotated data.
